mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates accommodative monetary policy that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days without regime dependence.
failure_condition: Average 20-day forward returns following FEDFUNDS < 3.5% are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) over any 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeding 4.5% signals labor market deterioration and reduced corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: Average 5-day forward returns following UNRATE > 4.5% are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent declines in housing starts (HOUST) and real consumption (RSAFS) indicate broad-based demand contraction, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days through reduced corporate revenue expectations.
failure_condition: Average 60-day forward returns following simultaneous HOUST and RSAFS declines are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime, rising industrial production (INDPRO) signals potential overheating and monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In late-cycle expansion (INDPRO growth > 1.5% annually, UNRATE < 5%), average 20-day returns following INDPRO rises are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) over any 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) indicates strengthening labor market conditions that support consumer spending and corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days without regime dependence.
failure_condition: Average 5-day forward returns following PAYEMS increases are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Year-over-year CPI exceeding 2.5% (CPIAUCSL) signals persistent inflation that may trigger monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Average 60-day forward returns following CPIAUCSL y/y > 2.5% are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) over any 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and year-over-year CPI above 2.5% (CPIAUCSL) indicate aggressive monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Average 20-day forward returns following FEDFUNDS increases and CPIAUCSL y/y > 2.5% are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a post-recession recovery regime, rising real GDP (GDPC1) signals sustained economic expansion and corporate earnings growth, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: In post-recession recovery (GDP growth > 2% annually, UNRATE < 6%), average 5-day forward returns following GDPC1 increases are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) over any 3-year rolling window.
